records.finding: The BLB5 logs and stone-tool work marks are documented. Associated Acheulean artefacts and experimental matches constrain the tool class, but no particular tool or existing catalogue record is identified as doing the work. Oldowan/Gona flaking and the later Hemudu and Altscherbitz construction records have different contexts. Site C North is a separate sequence.

records.finding: Proposed a dated field description of the bench in Shelter 1, assigned to Early Natufian Layer II by Haklay and Gopher. The original laboratory identification of calcined plaster in a bench-like feature at the site remains undated and may concern a different feature. The new event adds architectural use to the existing adhesive, interpreted hearth and burial-plaster evidence.

records.next: Find the collection record for sample 86-1 and test whether it identifies the bench in Shelter 1.

records.finding: Extended the existing settlement evidence with Building 1 traces consistent with roof access and a blocked ground-level doorway at Building 3. No separately dated Anatolian prerequisite or transmission is established. A lime-plaster floor sample from Çatalhöyük has unknown building level and cannot be linked to the suspected ladder trace or to the Levantine process by resemblance.

sources.note: Original Building 1 excavation report. The ladder and route are archaeological interpretations of plaster curvature and trampling.
Excavated doorway behind plaster gives a counterexample for at least some phases.
Original analysis identifies a lime plaster floor sample whose level is unknown.

records.next: Seek preserved ladder or stair fabric and an independently dated material or tool record from its specific context.

records.finding: Uruk's economic signs and its built settlement have a shared context. The oldest Eanna tablets largely come from secondary debris used to level later building platforms. This does not identify the responsible household or a direction between administration and urban growth. The existing kiln-fired brick record documents later use and is distinct from mud brick. No new edge.

sources.note: Nissen’s reanalysis explains the secondary contexts and uncertain original source of tablets. His attribution to stores of an administrative unit is qualified.
Site and period context for monumental mud-brick construction and administrative records. Institutional synthesis.

records.next: Seek construction-phase records or in situ tablet contexts that identify how an administrative practice materially supported a specific phase of urban building.

records.finding: Added a separate Well 116 event at Kissonerga-Mylouthkia. Three seeds from fills 123 and 124 are summarised by the 2003 excavation report as approximately 8600–8200 cal BCE. This anchors earlier well evidence while leaving the digging date approximate. Well 133 retains its original distinct date. Earlier publications recalibrate the same seed samples. Formal similarities with Shillourokambos, Atlit-Yam or later central European wells do not identify a transmission route.

sources.note: Final excavator report with sample identifiers, stratigraphy and explicit approximate range.
Earlier calibration of the same short-lived samples. Do not count it as independent radiocarbon evidence.

records.next: Inspect independently dated shaft construction levels at Shillourokambos and original mainland well features before claiming a shared construction lineage.

records.finding: Hemudu timber components document local carpentry. The individually examined posts at nearby Tianluoshan document timber construction in a related settlement, with their own context. Neither comparison establishes transfer of a particular joint. Eastern Saxon Altscherbitz is a different, distant use of mortise-and-tenon joinery. The primary 1978 Hemudu excavation report was identified but its full text was unavailable in this lane.

records.finding: Proposed a site-level uses_process link for a bench-like architectural feature at Eynan based on the direct laboratory identification of calcined plaster. The dated field description of the Shelter 1 bench is a separate observation. The link has no phase or event assignment. The sample's identity, the feature's function and any role of plaster in the transition to sedentary life remain unresolved.

records.finding: Proposed a timber-preparation uses_process edge and a distinct regional production record. Altscherbitz preserved oak beams split radially and tangentially. Ostrov has separately excavated, earlier split oak planks from a grooved-post well, documenting the technique as a practice distinct from wedged tenon assembly. Tegel co-authored both studies, which examine different physical assemblages. The link is anchored to local beam use and does not assert transmission between sites.

Modern trials reconstruct log splitting and the Altscherbitz frame. They use the earlier excavation as a comparator, so they test feasibility without identifying the actual ancient tool.

records.finding: Bronocice's associated dated material supports a vehicle depiction. Contemporary imagery in other Funnel Beaker settlements and physical tracks at Flintbek independently establish additional witnesses, leaving origin, direction and the specific construction or motive power behind the Bronocice image unsettled. Do not link the much later Sintashta horse traction or the different Mesopotamian potter's wheel on resemblance or sequence.

records.next: Seek a securely associated local wheel, axle or other vehicle remains. Compare independently dated contact and material evidence before inferring transmission.
